messages:
Maya: seeing a spike of 401s from hosted-api customers since 08:00 UTC, started getting support tickets. :rotating_light:
Jordan: yep getting the same. Metrics show auth-service 5xxs around 07:58 and then back to 200 but clients keep getting 401s. any recent key rotation?
Sam: rolling key rotation started at 07:55 in region us-west-2 (auto-rotate job). No alerts from rotation job.
Priya: support churn: customers report 'invalid_api_key' or 'insufficient_scope' depending on endpoint. Some keys work intermittently.
Maya: quick dump from proxy logs for one failing request: 
```
time=2026-03-15T07:59:18Z method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=401 upstream=auth-service error="invalid signature" api_key=redacted
```
Jordan: got a traceback from auth-service: 
```
AuthError: key not found for kid 'k-7a3'
 at verifySignature (jwt.go:142)
 at handler (auth_http.go:88)
```
Ned (oncall): I'm jumping in. Oncall runbook step1: check key rotation job logs, step2: check jwks cache TTL and propagation.
Sam: rotation job logs show a partial rollout — edge nodes updated keys but control-plane didn't propagate entries to short-lived jwks cache for a subset of instances. I see retries but they succeeded; however cache invalidation TTL was set to 15m. Some instances kept old cache entries until TTL expiry.
Priya: that should cause old keys to still be accepted, not missing keys. Why 'key not found'?
Jordan: digging — the rotation job accidentally removed the intermediate key set entry before the new key was published, creating a brief window where JWKS endpoint returned incomplete keys. Timeline: remove old -> publish new - but some replicas hit the endpoint during the window.
Maya: support stack traces show a mix of errors: invalid signature, key not found, and a few 403 'scope denied' where tokens are accepted but scope lookup fails. Could be cache inconsistency in token introspection service too.
Sam: token-introspect service is reading keys from the same JWKS cache but has a different caching shard; its cache TTL is 30s while auth-service's cache TTL is 15m. Inconsistent TTLs plus partial JWKS response explains varied symptoms.
Ned (oncall): immediate mitigation: roll back to previous key set (re-add removed entry) and stop the rotation job. Can someone push that?
Priya: re-adding key now. Patch applied to JWKS origin to include previous kid again.
deploy-bot: deploy started by Priya - jwks-origin revert v1.2.3 -> v1.2.2
Jordan: seeing JWKS origin now returns both kids. Instances that fetched after this return OK. But clients that hit instances which still have stale caches need either cache flush or restart.
Maya: support note: advise affected customers to retry; we already set rate limit retry window. But large customers still experiencing failures. Need faster remediation for stale caches.
Sam: options: 1) force cache flush on all auth-service instances via admin endpoint, 2) restart instances (painful), 3) bump TTL to 1s and let caches repopulate gradually. I prefer 1.
Ned (oncall): do cache flush now. Priya, can you call admin flush on auth-service?
Priya: hitting admin flush endpoint across regional fleets now (parallel). Command: 
```
for host in $(cat auth_hosts_us_west); do curl -XPOST https://$host/admin/cache/flush -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" & done
```
ops-bot: cache flush tasks enqueued (jobs: 42).
Jordan: watching metrics — auth-service 401s dropping. Support ticket volume dropping but some customers still hitting intermittent 401s.
Maya: one large customer reported billing broken because some requests didn't get through and they hit quota thresholds. Need a post-incident plan for customer reimbursements and message to CS.
Priya: noted — I'll prepare a draft for CS: root cause rotation window + cache TTL mismatch.
Sam: technical postmortem notes: rotation job assumed atomic swap semantics on JWKS origin but code performed remove then add. Need to change to publish-new-then-deprecate-old or ensure origin supports atomic replace. Also unify cache TTL across auth-stack to avoid inconsistent behavior.
Jordan: also add pre-check: after rotation publish, validate JWKS contains both keys for at least 2*cacheTTL across all origins before removing old.
Ned (oncall): immediate follow-ups: 1) change rotation to publish-first in next deploy (high priority), 2) add canary/observability rule: if 401 rate increases by >3x in 5m during rotation, auto-pause rotation, 3) run a sweep to find other services with inconsistent jwks TTL values.
Maya: setting urgent ticket for infra and runtime teams. Sam, Jordan, Priya please include exact repro steps and logs.
Sam: repro steps I used: 
1) run local JWKS origin with remove-then-add sequence
2) set auth-service cache TTL to 15m and token-introspect to 30s
3) fire load where some auth requests hit origin during the gap -> you'll see 401s with 'key not found'
Command snippet: 
```
# emulate gap
curl -XPOST http://jwks-origin/admin/remove-kid -d '{"kid":"k-old"}'
sleep 3
curl -XPOST http://jwks-origin/admin/add-kid -d '{"kid":"k-new", "pub":"..."}'
# then spike requests to auth endpoint
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://auth-gw/v1/embeddings & done
```
Jordan: logs to attach for postmortem: rotation-job logs, jwks-origin audit (remove/add events), auth-service cache hits/misses, proxy traces showing 401s, and support complain transcripts.
Priya: draft message for CS: 
"We experienced an auth outage affecting some API keys around 07:58 UTC due to a key rotation process that briefly removed key material from the JWKS origin before the new key was fully published. This created a window where some auth instances returned 401s. We have reverted the JWKS origin, flushed caches, and paused rotations. Engineers are implementing a safer publish-first rotation and unified cache TTLs. We will follow up with impacted customers about credits."
Maya: add: customers who saw billing anomalies should open case with billing team. We'll proactively reach out to top 5 impacted accounts.
Ned (oncall): putting an incident page together and assigning owners. Priority P2 -> escalate to P1 if customer revenue impact > $X.
Jordan: change-list for next week: 
- rotation: atomic publish-first (Sam)
- observability: 401 surge alert during rotations (Jordan)
- infra: unify JWKS cache TTLs across services (Priya)
- support: templated customer outreach and credit policy (Maya)

Maya: thanks everyone. I'll close the thread when postmortem doc is up. :white_check_mark:
Maya: postmortem link (draft): https://internal.redwood.com/postmortems/1935043210-jwks-rotation-cache-gap (will update)
